segments.text: Hi, I'm Jennifer Evangelista, a data engineering and solutions architecture specialist from Brazil. This is Shield, a data quality teammate that lives in your team chat, built on Switch.

Here is an incident I wrote about. Every job ran green this morning, but it was a backfill for last week. The gate only asked whether the jobs ran today, not which business date they processed, so last week's numbers were about to ship as today's.

Shield is a custom agent on the Switch agent protocol. Switch turns a Mattermost channel into a room with the engineer and Shield, delivers only the messages that mention Shield, and keeps an audit document in the room. Shield runs a Great Expectations contract, the business date gate from my article, reads owners and lineage from an OpenMetadata shaped catalog, and uses Gemma, a small open model running locally, to explain the impact.

I seed that exact incident on a fictional warehouse and ask Shield to scan. It sees that the runs were green for October twenty ninth, not November fifth. It lists everything downstream with its owners, and proposes a fix: hold the eight o'clock report and re-run today's partition. Nothing changes yet.
I approve in the channel. Shield holds the dashboard, re-runs the three jobs for the right business date, checks again, and because the check now passes, it puts the report back on schedule.

Not every problem can be fixed from here. When a producer renames a column, Shield proposes holding the report and notifying the owners. After I approve, it records an incident in the catalog, and it says plainly that the check still fails until the producer restores the contract.

Duplicate keys get a dedupe, confirmed by a fresh check. And I stay in charge. This null spike comes from a test load I know about, so I reject the finding with a reason, and Shield leaves the data alone.
Every scan, approval, rejection and fix lands in the audit trail, with who did it and when. It is in the chat, and it is a document attached to the Switch room.

Everything is reproducible. One script starts Switch with its bundled Mattermost. A bootstrap registers Shield and creates the room. Forty two unit tests cover the checks, and an end to end test runs the whole conversation through Switch on a fresh GitHub runner.
Shield does the checking and the explaining. People make the call, in the chat they already use. Thanks for watching.
